primitives.name: Obstructed Will
primitives.verbatim_quote: The exhausted sailor on a wreck has a will which is obstructed.
primitives.assumptions: The will is a directed mental force. Obstruction occurs when external constraints (e.g., exhaustion) interfere with its execution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the cost of action exceeds the perceived benefit, the will collapses into passive endurance.

layer2.mapping: GSI - A gambler's will is obstructed by adverse odds, leading to forced passivity.
layer2.telemetry: Observed shift from active betting to holding current position.

primitives.name: Inhibitory Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: Rather the aching toil !" he says; and it becomes reality then, in spite of the inhibiting influence of the relatively luxurious sensations which he gets from lying still.
primitives.assumptions: Luxurious sensations (e.g., comfort) act as a negative feedback loop against the drive to pump water.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Sensory comfort reduces the urgency of the task, causing the sailor to remain inert.

layer2.mapping: GSE - Inhibitory neurotransmitters prevent motor cortex activation, halting planned actions.

When the sailor chooses to endure pain rather than accept death, his will is redirected from survival to suffering. This redirection is mathematically modeled as a bifurcation: the system settles into a stable equilibrium where continued exertion minimizes a Lyapunov function representing total energy expenditure. In the insomnia example, monotone sensory input reduces cognitive entropy, forcing the nervous system toward a sleep attractor. Willful suppression operates via a top-down control signal that modifies synaptic gain, effectively flattening the response to chaotic stimuli. These primitives describe how agents navigate constrained state spaces under opposing motivational gradients.
